candidates.computation_change_reason: Constituent identity determines which parameter-specific discharge limits (A), monitoring requirements (B), and missing-evidence/no-result cases (C) are evaluated for reported measurements.

CAS registry number may be used to match this row to facility measurements or permit schedules; a different parameter match would change which limits, monitoring obligations, and evidence gaps are attributed to reported results.

Without column headers, this numeric value could represent an enforceable limit, a calculation input, or a non-operative reference value; treating it as an applicable limit versus another column role changes which numeric standard is used for exceedance determination.

This value appears multiple times in the row and may denote period- or outfall-specific effluent limits from a reasonable-potential analysis; interpreting which occurrence applies to a given monitoring period, or whether it is operative versus illustrative, changes the enforceable limit selected for compliance comparison.

Large placeholder magnitudes in limit tables are often read as indicating no numeric limit or unlimited discharge rather than a literal enforceable value; whether 1E+100 is treated as absent limit, report-only, or a real cap changes whether numeric exceedance analysis runs (A) and how no-result or non-comparable periods are classified (C).

This calculated-looking magnitude may be a derived reasonable-potential limit, a background concentration, or a non-enforceable analytical output; assigning it operative limit status versus supporting analysis only changes which numeric standard applies to measurements.

As with adjacent derived values, interpreting this number as an enforceable discharge limit versus an intermediate calculation result changes whether and against what value reported manganese results are compared.

Terminal N/A may mean monitoring not required, no numeric limit applies, no discharge occurred, or data were not provided; different readings change whether a compliance limit is selected (A), whether monitoring was obligatory (B), and whether the period is documented no-discharge, conditionally exempt, or unresolved missing evidence (C).
